title: Service commands for a room's policy and the clients behind its users
description:
IRC's MODE and NAMES are narrower than what MIMI rooms carry, so two things a user may reasonably ask cannot be asked.

ROOM POLICY. room-policy-04 gives a room roles with capabilities, a preauth list, fixed_membership, parent_dependent, max_users, max_clients and multi_device. IRC MODE carries a handful of letters and mimid maps what it can (CHANNEL_MODES, PARAMETER_MODES in the front end). Everything else is invisible, including the two facts that change what a user may do: whether the room's membership is fixed, and what their own role allows. A user who cannot invite should be able to find out why.

CLIENTS BEHIND A USER. NAMES lists nicks, and a nick is a MIMI user. A user has clients, and may have none while remaining a participant, which is exactly the state room-policy-04 §5 leaves a user in when they remove their devices from a DM. So NAMES can show a participant who cannot receive anything, with no way to tell. mimi-protocol-07's participant and client lists have the data.

WHAT TO ADD: two service commands, one for a room's policy as mimid evaluated it, one for the clients behind each participant of a room. Both read-only.

DO NOT WIDEN MODE OR NAMES TO CARRY THIS. Stock clients parse both and mis-render unexpected content, which is the epic's rule; and a MODE letter invented for fixed_membership would collide with the next network a user connects to.

CHECK AGAINST THE EVALUATOR, NOT THE WIRE: mimi-room-policy evaluates policy and documents what it does not check, including §5's rule on leaving and the max_clients, max_users and multi_device limits (decision mimid-1wgh.3.50). A command that prints a limit mimid does not enforce must say so, or it tells the user a constraint protects them when it does not.
